title: Making a Piecewise Function Continuous at the Origin
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine the value of c that makes f(x, y) = sin(x^2 + y^2) / (x^2 + y^2) for (x, y) != (0, 0) and f(0, 0) = c continuous everywhere.

steps.title: Substitute Single Variable u = x^2 + y^2
steps.explanation: Rephrase the 2D limit as a 1D radial limit.

steps.title: Evaluate Known Fundamental Limit
steps.why: Finding the limiting value at the origin.

steps.title: Enforce Continuity Definition
steps.mathExpression: f(0, 0) = c = \lim_{(x, y) \to (0, 0)} f(x, y) = 1 \implies c = 1
steps.explanation: For continuity, the defined value must match the limiting value.
